title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Internal Tools
author: Ava Chen
body:
Overview

This document provides a concise, single-source reference for new and existing employees about what it means to work at Redwood Inference. It covers role families and career ladders, core benefits and perks, our hiring and onboarding process, and the primary internal tools you will use day-to-day. Where appropriate, sections include ownership, step-by-step procedures, and links to related pages.

1) Working at Redwood — principles and culture

Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on delivering production-grade inference. Our cultural principles:
- Customer empathy: solve for predictable, reliable inference in production.
- Ship with quality: testable, observable, and measurable releases.
- Ownership with collaboration: teams own outcomes, and knowledge is shared across squads.
- Continuous learning: we invest in research, tooling, and career development.

These principles inform hiring, performance evaluation, and career ladder design.

2) Roles and career ladders (quick reference)

High-level role families: engineering, product, research/applied ML, infra/SRE, design, sales/CS, people-ops, finance/legal. Each family shares the same level design (IC and manager tracks).

Example career ladder summary table (illustrative):

| Level | IC title example | Typical years | Expectations (summary) |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| IC1 | Software Engineer I | 0-2 | Contributes to code with guidance, writes tests, resolves low-complexity bugs.
| IC2 | Software Engineer II | 2-4 | Delivers major features, owns small services, collaborates across teams.
| IC3 | Senior Engineer | 4-7 | Leads design for medium complexity systems, mentors others, influences architecture.
| IC4 | Staff Engineer | 7+ | Drives cross-team technical strategy, high-complexity designs, measurable impact.
| Mgr1 | Engineering Manager I | N/A | Manages small team, coaching and delivery ownership.
| Mgr2 | Senior Manager | N/A | Manages managers or multiple teams, sets team strategy.

Detailed ladder documents are maintained per discipline (see related_pages). Promotion criteria emphasize impact, breadth, leadership, and mentorship. Promotion checklist (for managers and candidates):
1. Document top 3 impact examples (with metrics where possible).
2. Gather peer feedback (at least 3 independent reviewers).
3. Manager writes calibration note comparing candidate to level rubric.
4. Submit packet to People Ops using the promotions template (link in related pages).

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Core benefits (standard plan unless noted):
- Health: medical, dental, and vision with multiple plan tiers and HSA options. Redwood covers 80% of employee-only premiums and subsidizes family coverage.
- Paid time off: 20 days PTO accrual per year (prorated first year), 10 company holidays, flexible parental leave (primary: 16 weeks, secondary: 10 weeks).
- Financial: 401(k) with company match up to 4% of salary; competitive equity grants at hire and refresh cycles.
- Professional development: $2,000 annual learning stipend and dedicated Maker Days each quarter.
- Wellbeing: monthly wellness stipend, EAP program, and access to mental health coaching.
- Remote / work-from-office: hybrid-first policy by default; some teams (e.g., infra, hardware) may require regular office presence. See team-specific expectations on team pages.

Perks and operational details:
- Equipment: standard workstation allowance at hire and refresh every 3 years. For dedicated hardware requests (GPU laptops, external monitors), submit via IT ticket.
- Conference and travel policy: pre-approval required; travel guidelines are in the Finance Travel playbook.
- Stipends for home office setup are processed through People Ops.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring philosophy
- We bias for clear evidence of craftsmanship, curious problem-solving, and ability to work with observability-first behaviors. We hire for potential and demonstrated impact.

Recruiting process (standard individual contributor role)
1. Resume screen by recruiting.
2. Recruiter phone screen (culture, role expectations, logistics).
3. Hiring manager technical screen (30-45 min).
4. Work sample or take-home (role-dependent).
5. On-site loop: 4 interviews (design, coding, systems, team fit).
6. Debrief and hiring committee review.
7. Offer and reference checks.

Interview best practices for panelists
- Use structured rubrics. Score on problem-solving, communication, ownership, and role-specific skills.
- Document clear feedback within 48 hours.
- Disclose reasonable timeline expectations to candidates.

New hire onboarding checklist (people-ops + manager responsibilities)
- Pre-boarding (People Ops): create accounts (email, Slack, Redwood Console), prepare hardware, enroll in benefits, confirm start date.
- Day 0-1 (Manager): welcome message, team intro, first-week schedule, assign buddy.
- Week 1: operational ramps (accesses, CI/CD orientation, key repos), first 1:1 with manager, small starter tickets.
- Month 1: first project milestone, check-in on role clarity and goals.
- Month 3: formal onboarding review (expectations, feedback, growth plan).

Templates and quick links are available in the onboarding playbook (see related_pages).

5) Internal tools guide — primers and quick commands

Primary systems you will use:
- Slack: primary async communication. Channels are organized by org and project. Use #oncall for urgent SRE needs.
- Redwood Console (internal): fast access to route dashboards, model metrics, and billing insights.
- GitHub: source control and PR workflows. Use the standard PR template.
- Jira: ticketing for delivery and incident tracking (project boards per squad).
- PagerDuty: on-call rotations and escalation. Follow the oncall runbook when paged.
- Internal Wiki / Confluence: canonical docs for runbooks, architecture, and standards.

Sample commands and snippets
- Git: create a feature branch and push:
  git checkout -b feat/<your-name>/<short-description>
  git commit -m "feat: add ..."
  git push --set-upstream origin feat/<your-name>/<short-description>

- Console API token retrieval (CLI):
  export REDWOOD_TOKEN=$(rbx auth token --user $EMAIL)
  rbx models list --token $REDWOOD_TOKEN

- Quick health check for a service (kubectl example):
  kubectl get pods -n <team-namespace> -l app=<service>
  kubectl logs -f <pod-name> -c runtime

Security and access notes
- Access requests: submit to the access-and-permissions queue. All privileged access requires manager approval and MFA.
- Secrets: use the company KMS; never check secrets into Git. See Secure SDLC page for dev-time guidance.

6) Performance reviews and growth planning

Cadence and expectations
- Performance reviews are on a twice-yearly cadence (mid-year and year-end), with ongoing 1:1 coaching.
- Self-assessment required two weeks prior to the review window. Managers provide written feedback and a development plan.

Career conversations
- Employees are encouraged to create a 12-month growth plan with manager and seek stretch opportunities across programs (mentorship, cross-team projects, leadership of small initiatives). People Ops runs promotion calibration sessions twice per year.

7) Ownership, escalation, and contacts

Document ownership: People Ops maintains this handbook. Suggested updates should be sent to people-ops@redwood.com.

Escalation path for urgent people issues:
1. Manager
2. HR Business Partner (see People Ops directory)
3. Head of People Ops (for unresolved/serious cases)

8) Frequently asked questions

Q: Who approves flexible work exceptions?
A: Your manager in partnership with People Ops. Team-level office expectations are set by the hiring manager.

Q: How do I request additional equipment?
A: File an IT request with justification; managers approve purchases above the standard allowance.

Q: Where are the payroll and tax documents?
A: Finance self-service portal (internal link in related_pages).

9) Revision history
